title: Mitre Lecture: Professor Chris Lintott on the search for extraterrestrial life
excerpt: Discover Professor Chris Lintott’s Mitre Lecture at Trinity School, exploring the search for extraterrestrial life.
content:
We were delighted to welcome Professor Chris Lintott to Trinity for our first Mitre Lecture of the new academic year. His insightful lecture entitled “Is it Aliens? Looking for Weird in the Cosmos” explored the ongoing search for extraterrestrial life.

Professor Lintott is a Professor of Astrophysics at the University of Oxford and is best known for his work on the BBC television show ‘The Sky at Night’ as well as being the author of several books.

Taking the audience into the world of astrophysics, Professor Lintott shared some exciting discoveries. He revealed that over the course of a week his team had discovered roughly five thousand new asteroids, explaining that in the next year they are set to find around five million new objects in the solar system.

Professor Lintott explained that part of his role in studying the newly discovered objects would be to see if any of them have any unusual characteristics, leaving the audience with the fascinating thought that “if there are, it’s possible they might be alien spacecraft.”

Following the lecture, two Lower Sixth students, Eshan and Otto, sat down with Professor Lintott to lead an exciting questions-and-answers session, giving guests and students alike a chance to ask the big questions. Among the questions raised were:

“What if the question is not where are the aliens but when are the aliens?”

“If you did find alien life, what would you do about it?”

“If aliens were to use transport in space using non-metals, like elements you would commonly detect like rocks on other planets, would you be able to detect it?”

Eshan commented, “I think the lecture was very interesting. It looked at all the odd things in the universe and questioned whether it was aliens, before introducing other explanations. Through repeating this, Professor Lintott showed us how difficult the search for aliens is. I really enjoyed this talk because the speaker had genuine passion for his work in astrophysics and this spread to the crowd, making us all interested. I learnt a lot about how we search for extraterrestrial life, from how the media always jump the gun and say we have found aliens to how astrophysicists publish papers and have to come up with a hypothesis. I’m always excited to go to the Mitre Lectures as they never fail to pique my curiosity and this was another great talk.”

Mr Dabby, Assistant Head – Teaching and Learning, added: “The Oxford astrophysicist Professor Chris Lintott, known to many for his work as presenter of the BBC’s The Sky at Night, delivered a fascinating lecture on astrophysics and the search for life in the universe, including insights into discoveries announced just a week earlier. An engaging Q&A session followed, led by two of our Sixth Form scientists. Professor Lintott kindly signed copies of his books, The Crowd and the Cosmos and Our Accidental Universe: Stories of Discovery from Asteroids to Aliens, which are now available for students to borrow from the library. We are very grateful to Professor Lintott for providing such an inspiring start to this year’s Mitre Lecture Series.”
